examples.en: The employer has to pay wages on time.
The new employer is kind to the staff.
The employer and the employee wrote up a contract.

examples.ko: 그는 고용주를 잘 만나서 일이 편해요.
examples.en: He got a good employer, so his work is easy.

examples.ko: 고용주가 바뀌면 근무 조건도 달라질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the employer changes, working conditions can change too.

examples.ko: 외국인 직원의 고용주는 비자 서류를 준비해야 해요.
examples.en: The employer of a foreign worker has to prepare the visa documents.

explain: 일하는 사람은 '근로자'나 '직원'이에요. 일상에서는 보통 '사장님'이라고 부르고, '고용주'는 법, 계약, 뉴스에서 쓰는 말이에요. 사람을 직접 부를 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: The other side is '근로자' or '직원'. In daily life people say '사장님', and '고용주' belongs to law, contracts, and news. You never use it to address someone directly.

examples.en: I check the help-wanted column in the newspaper every morning.
I saw a posting in the help-wanted column and called.

examples.ko: 이 사이트는 구인란이 따로 있어서 편해요.
examples.en: This site has a separate help-wanted section, so it's convenient.

examples.ko: 동네 가게 구인란에서 아르바이트 자리를 찾았어요.
examples.en: I found a part-time job in the local shops' help-wanted listings.

examples.ko: 요즘은 구인란보다 앱으로 일자리를 찾는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: These days, more people look for jobs through apps than through help-wanted columns.

examples.ko: 이 앱의 구인란은 누구나 무료로 이용할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Anyone can use this app's help-wanted section for free.

explain: 신문이나 웹사이트에서 사람을 구하는 공고가 모여 있는 칸에 써요. 요즘은 '구인 공고'나 '채용 공고'라는 말도 많이 써요. 일자리를 찾는 사람 쪽 말은 '구직'이에요.
explain_en: It is used for the section of a newspaper or website where job postings are gathered. These days people also say '구인 공고' or '채용 공고'. The word for the side of people looking for work is '구직'.

examples.ko: 새 사장님은 젊은 인재를 적극적으로 등용했어요.
examples.en: The new president actively appointed young talent.

examples.ko: 임금은 능력 있는 사람을 관리로 등용했어요.
examples.en: The king appointed capable people as officials.

examples.ko: 정부가 여성 전문가를 장관으로 등용할 거래요.
examples.en: They say the government will appoint a female expert as minister.

examples.ko: 학벌보다 실력을 보고 사람을 등용해야 해요.
examples.en: You should appoint people based on ability, not on school background.

examples.ko: 그 감독은 신인 선수를 과감히 등용해서 성공했어요.
examples.en: The coach boldly used a rookie player and succeeded.

examples.ko: 새 대표가 외부 인사를 등용하자 말이 많았어요.
examples.en: When the new CEO brought in an outsider, there was a lot of talk.

explain: '뽑다, 쓰다'와 비슷하지만 능력 있는 사람을 중요한 자리에 앉힌다는 느낌이 강해요. 회사에서 사람을 뽑을 때는 '채용하다'가 더 자연스러워요. 뉴스나 역사 이야기에서 '인재를 등용하다'로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is similar to '뽑다' or '쓰다' but strongly suggests putting a capable person into an important post. For ordinary hiring at a company, '채용하다' sounds more natural. It often appears in news and history as '인재를 등용하다'.

examples.ko: 회사에서 한 달 무급 휴가를 받았어요.
examples.en: I got a month of unpaid leave from the company.
Wouldn't an unpaid internship be tough?
This job is unpaid, so I'm hesitating.
He helped with the volunteer work without pay.
Making people work unpaid breaks the law.
My child was sick, so I took a few unpaid days off.

explain: '무급'의 반대말은 '유급'이에요. 보통 '무급 휴가', '무급 인턴'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여서 써요. 월급을 받는 휴가는 '유급 휴가'라고 해요.
explain_en: The opposite of '무급' is '유급', meaning paid. It usually sits in front of another noun, as in '무급 휴가' (unpaid leave) and '무급 인턴' (unpaid intern).

en: arrange; broker; help find (a job, housing)

examples.en: The district office helps find jobs for senior citizens.

examples.ko: 이 센터는 유학생에게 집을 알선하기도 해요.
examples.en: This center also arranges housing for international students.

examples.ko: 선배가 아르바이트 자리를 알선해 줘서 고마웠어요.
examples.en: I was thankful that my senior helped me find a part-time job.
The travel agency said it would arrange a hotel for us.
The company arranged a dormitory for the new employees.

examples.ko: 돈을 받고 알선하는 사람은 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: You should be careful with people who arrange things for money.

explain: 중간에서 사람과 일자리, 집 같은 것을 이어 주는 일에 써요. 기관이나 업체가 주어일 때 자연스럽고, 친구 사이에서는 보통 '소개해 주다'라고 해요. '일자리 알선', '알선 업체'처럼 명사로도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when someone in the middle connects people with things like jobs or housing. It sounds natural with an organization or business as the subject, while between friends people usually say '소개해 주다'. It also appears as a noun, as in '일자리 알선' and '알선 업체'.

examples.en: I got a job offer from another company.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 유럽 팀에서 오퍼가 왔어요.
examples.en: That player got an offer from a European team.

examples.ko: 오퍼 조건을 보고 며칠 더 생각해 볼게요.
examples.en: I'll look at the terms of the offer and think about it a few more days.
The offer arrived by email first.
The salary was low, so I turned down the offer.

examples.ko: 친구가 해외 회사의 오퍼에 대해 물어봤어요.
examples.en: My friend asked me about an offer from a company abroad.

explain: 한국에서는 취업, 이적, 계약 이야기에서 영어 그대로 '오퍼'를 많이 써요. 보통 '오퍼를 받다', '오퍼를 거절하다'처럼 말해요. 일상에서 무언가를 권할 때는 '제안'이나 '권하다'를 써요.
explain_en: In Korean, '오퍼' is used in English form when talking about jobs, transfers, and contracts. It is typically '오퍼를 받다' or '오퍼를 거절하다'. For offering something in everyday life, use '제안' or '권하다'.

examples.en: I'm being transferred to the Seoul head office next month.

examples.ko: 남편이 대구로 전근하는 바람에 같이 이사했어요.
examples.en: My husband was transferred to Daegu, so we moved together.
I heard the teacher has transferred to another school.
I transferred to this branch two years ago.
After I transferred, commuting became much easier.

examples.ko: 해외로 전근하게 되면 가족도 같이 가야 할까요?
examples.en: If I get transferred overseas, should my family go with me?

explain: '전근하다'는 같은 곳 안에서 근무지를 옮기는 것이라 '이직하다'와 달라요. 높일 때는 '전근하시다'라고 해요. 말할 때는 '전근 가다'도 자주 써요.
explain_en: 전근하다 means moving to a different workplace within the same organization, so it differs from '이직하다'. The honorific form is '전근하시다'. In speech, '전근 가다' is also often used.

examples.en: That department head was demoted to a regional branch.

examples.ko: 실수 한 번 때문에 좌천될 수도 있어요.
examples.en: One mistake could get you demoted.

examples.ko: 그는 본사에서 작은 사무소로 좌천돼서 힘들어했어요.
examples.en: He was sent from headquarters to a small office and had a hard time.
Even after being demoted, he kept working hard.
There's a rumor that he fought with the boss and got demoted.

examples.ko: 좌천되면 어떤 기분일지 상상도 안 돼요.
examples.en: I can't even imagine how it feels to be demoted.

explain: '승진하다'의 반대로, 지위가 낮아지거나 중요하지 않은 곳으로 밀려날 때 써요. 단순한 '전근'과 달리 벌이나 불이익이라는 느낌이 강해요. 일상에서는 '밀려나다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '승진하다' (to be promoted) and is used when someone's rank drops or they are pushed to a less important place. Unlike a plain transfer, it carries a feeling of punishment or disadvantage. In daily talk people also say '밀려나다'.

examples.en: I was introduced to a job at an employment agency.
I went to an employment agency and got a consultation.
This employment agency doesn't charge a fee.
I found a part-time job through the local employment agency.
The employment agency staff explained things kindly.
I submitted my resume to the employment agency and am waiting for a call.

explain: 일자리를 찾는 사람과 사람을 구하는 곳을 이어 주는 곳이에요. 요즘은 '취업 사이트'나 '앱'으로 구하는 사람도 많아서 일상 대화에서는 '일자리 구하다'라고 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is a place that connects people looking for work with employers who need workers. These days many people use job sites or apps, so in everyday talk they more often say '일자리 구하다' (look for a job).
